exam_name: CFE Part 4: Fraud Prevention and Deterrence
passing_score_scale: Percentage (75% passing score required per part)
exam_format: Linear (fixed-form, 4 sequential parts — Pearson VUE or online proctored)

testing_centers.notes: Available at Pearson VUE testing centers worldwide. Online proctored option available via ACFE ProctorU. ACFE membership and exam eligibility must be confirmed before scheduling.
Online proctored option available directly through ACFE's ProctorU integration. Requires stable internet connection and compatible webcam.

id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. Name on ID must match ACFE membership registration exactly.
exam_rules: No personal items, notes, or reference materials permitted. Calculator provided on-screen where applicable. All 4 parts must be passed; parts may be taken in any order. Candidates have 30 months from ACFE approval to pass all 4 parts. ACFE membership must remain active throughout the exam process.
renewal_options: CFE credential requires active ACFE membership renewal every 2 years. 20 CPE hours required annually, including 10 hours in fraud-related topics. Renewal handled through ACFE member portal.

prerequisites.description: Part of the full CFE Exam; ACFE membership required

retake_policy.notes: 30-day waiting period between failed attempts on the same part. Each retake requires payment of the per-part retake fee. Candidates have 30 months total to pass all 4 parts after initial approval.

editorial.meta_description: The CFE Fraud Prevention examination evaluates candidates using 125 questions with a required passing score of 75 percent and a duration of 135 minutes.
editorial.overview: The CFE Part 4 Fraud Prevention and Deterrence examination comprehensively evaluates candidate proficiency across five distinct domains. Candidates are given a strict duration of 135 minutes to answer 125 multiple-choice questions delivered in a linear format through Pearson VUE or online proctored testing. A passing score of 75 percent is required.
editorial.who_should_take: Certified Fraud Examiner candidates and anti-fraud professionals studying fraud prevention, deterrence principles, anti-corruption compliance frameworks, and corporate governance standards required in the modern anti-fraud industry today.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Carefully review the official candidate handbooks and detailed content outlines concerning the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, anti-bribery provisions, accounting rules, and compliance program standards. Understand statutory definitions, regulatory enforcement practices, and corporate liability principles across all assigned domains for the test to ensure comprehensive mastery of the subject matter.

domain_guidance.summary: Examines the core concepts of why fraud occurs through the Fraud Triangle framework, analyzing motives, pressures, and opportunities within organizational environments to understand illicit behavior and deter workplace schemes.

Covers fraud risk management strategies, focusing on identifying, assessing, and mitigating organizational fraud risks through internal controls, governance policies, and structured evaluation methodologies designed to protect corporate assets.

Focuses on ethics programs, corporate codes of conduct, and establishing an organizational culture that promotes integrity and discourages illicit behavior through clear administrative policies and internal reporting systems.

Explores the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and related anti-corruption laws, detailing anti-bribery provisions, accounting controls, and jurisdictional conduct applicable to multinational corporate entities operating in global business environments.

Analyzes criminology theory to understand the underlying behavioral and sociological factors that drive individuals to commit white-collar crimes, occupational fraud, and various organizational financial offenses against their employers.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Review all testing rules before your appointment, ensuring you arrive on time at the Pearson VUE center or set up your online proctored workstation to complete your examination.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The certification examination contains a total of 125 multiple-choice questions structured in a fixed, linear format that candidates must complete during their scheduled testing session.
A passing score of 75 percent is required per part on the certification exam to demonstrate adequate competency across all tested knowledge domains and subject areas.
Registered candidates are given a total duration of exactly 135 minutes to complete all of the multiple-choice questions included in the official test session successfully and efficiently.

faq.question_title: What question format is used on the test?
faq.answer_text: The test utilizes multiple-choice questions delivered securely via Pearson VUE test centers or through convenient online proctored testing options that are available to all qualified applicants.

methodology.summary: This informational page was built using official ACFE candidate handbooks, exam content outlines, and regulatory source documentation to provide accurate guidance for candidates.
